section_title: How should hope for the end shape life today?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 7 The end of all things is near. Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray. 8 Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins. 9 Show hospitality to one another without complaining.

context_lines: Peter’s statement that the end is near leads straight to ordinary faithfulness: clear thinking, prayer, deep love and cheerful hospitality. He does not give a date or tell the readers to stop caring for daily needs.

The saying about love covering many sins recalls [Proverbs 10:12](https://biblehub.com/bsb/proverbs/10.htm), where love is contrasted with hatred that stirs up conflict. Love changes how people respond to one another’s faults.
Hospitality gives that love a practical form. Welcoming others without complaining makes room for them in one’s life, rather than treating them only as a burden.
common_interpretation_lines: [Calvin](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/1_peter/4.htm) and [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-first-epistle-general-of-st-peter/) connect watchfulness with prayer and read the covering of sins in terms of generous love toward others. Calvin stresses forgiving rather than spreading faults; Wesley describes patient care and prayer for the other person.
Both take the approaching end as a reason for faithful living. Hope draws believers toward God and one another, rather than making mutual care less important.
god_plan_lines: In [Matthew 24:42–51](https://biblehub.com/bsb/matthew/24.htm), readiness for the Lord’s return is pictured through a servant faithfully caring for the household. Watching includes doing the work of care entrusted to him.

[Romans 12:9–13](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/12.htm) likewise joins sincere love, patience in affliction, persistent prayer and hospitality. These are ways the hope God gives takes shape in a community’s present life.
